sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0
sources.scope_and_limit: Recommendation 15 May 2025. Credentials express issuer claims; verification does not establish truth or resource authorization.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifiers v1.0
sources.scope_and_limit: Recommendation 19 July 2022. Identifier and verification-method framework; identity proofing, rotation and recovery depend on the chosen method and trust arrangements.

sources.title: Web Authentication Level 3
sources.scope_and_limit: Recommendation 25 August 2026. Public-key authentication; a successful ceremony alone does not prove understanding of business terms.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines
sources.scope_and_limit: Separates identity proofing, authentication and federation. Assurance choices require an application-specific assessment.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Demonstrating Proof of Possession RFC 9449
sources.scope_and_limit: Sender-constrained tokens; DPoP does not cover the request body or general headers and does not itself decide authorization.

sources.title: HTTP Message Signatures RFC 9421
sources.scope_and_limit: Signatures over selected HTTP components. Applications must choose and enforce the required coverage and replay controls.

sources.title: Digest Fields RFC 9530
sources.scope_and_limit: Content-Digest and Repr-Digest. A digest requires recomputation and authenticated binding; it is not an access grant.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange RFC 8693
sources.scope_and_limit: Delegation and impersonation are distinct. Revocation propagation is not an automatic property of token exchange.

sources.title: OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests RFC 9396
sources.scope_and_limit: Fine-grained authorization_details. WRN would need a defined application profile and permission-containment semantics.

sources.title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0 RFC 9162
sources.scope_and_limit: Experimental RFC. Merkle inclusion and consistency concepts; the specification explicitly identifies inconsistent log views as a limitation.

sources.title: Transparency Log Witness Protocol
sources.scope_and_limit: Version 1.1.0 observed. Witness cosignatures support checkpoint consistency; trust, independence and availability remain assumptions.

sources.title: Locking objects with Object Lock
sources.scope_and_limit: WORM protection applies to specified object versions; new versions and delete markers are still possible. Product example, not a required provider.

sources.title: Privacy and encryption
sources.scope_and_limit: Public IPFS exposes metadata; content requires application encryption for confidentiality. A content identifier is not an authorization credential.

sources.title: Persistence
sources.scope_and_limit: Availability requires retention, pinning and storage arrangements. Content addressing does not promise perpetual availability.

sources.title: Private Data
sources.scope_and_limit: Collection membership and distribution require explicit design; adding members can expose historical collection data. A ledger alone does not implement personal sharing rules.

sources.title: Selective Disclosure for JSON Web Tokens RFC 9901
sources.scope_and_limit: Standards Track RFC, November 2025. Selective claim disclosure does not by itself ensure unlinkability, truth or fresh authorization.

sources.title: Object Lock considerations
sources.scope_and_limit: Object Lock does not prevent loss or deletion of encryption keys; retained ciphertext can become unreadable. Recovery must protect decryption material separately.

sources.title: Building accountability into the Internet of Things The IoT Databox model
sources.scope_and_limit: Journal of Reliable Intelligent Environments 4, 39–55. Prior art for personal stores, app manifests, fine-grained consent, isolated processing and audit.

sources.title: SocialGenPod Privacy Friendly Generative AI Social Web Applications with Decentralised Personal Data Stores
sources.scope_and_limit: WWW 2024 Companion, 1067–1070. Prototype combining Solid personal stores, interchangeable LLMs and retrieval over permitted private documents.

sources.title: Zanzibar Googles Consistent Global Authorization System
sources.scope_and_limit: USENIX ATC 2019, 33–46. Authorization/content causal consistency. Reported Google performance must not be assigned to this proposed system.

sources.title: Do you Need a Blockchain
sources.scope_and_limit: CVCBT 2018, 45–54. Method for deciding between conventional storage, permissioned and permissionless systems based on trust and writers.

sources.title: Protecting privacy using the decentralized label model
sources.scope_and_limit: ACM TOSEM 9(4), 410–442. Information-flow labels and owner-controlled declassification; not a proof for unrestricted language-model outputs.

sources.title: Securing FTP with TLS RFC 4217
sources.scope_and_limit: Explains FTPS terminology. A secure transfer protocol is distinct from a personal identity or decentralized work platform.

sources.title: ERC 721 Non Fungible Token Standard
sources.scope_and_limit: Tracks and transfers token ownership. A separate application policy must determine any relationship between a token and data access.
